problems.problem: For what largest natural $n$ does there exist a set of $n$ natural numbers with the following property: among the numbers of the set exactly one number is divisible by $n$, exactly two numbers are divisible by $n-1$, and so on, exactly $n-1$ numbers of this set are divisible by 2, and all $n$ numbers are divisible by $1$?

The circle $\gamma$ is circumscribed about an acute-angled triangle $ABC$; $AD$ and $AL$ are its altitude and angle bisector, respectively. Denote by $W$, $T$, $A'$ the second points of intersection with the circle $\gamma$ of the lines $AL$, $WD$, $TL$, respectively. Prove that $AA'$ is a diameter of the circle $\gamma$.

Does there exist a geometric progression of natural numbers $b_0, b_1, \ldots, b_{2014}$ with common ratio different from $10$ satisfying the following condition: the number $b_{i+1}$ has in its decimal representation exactly one digit more than the number $b_i$, for all $i$ from 0 to 2013?

Let a connected graph with vertices $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n$ be given. Denote by $d_{i,j}$ the smallest number of edges that must be traversed to get from the vertex $A_i$ to the vertex $A_j$. Find the largest possible value of the sum $$D=\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}d_{i,j}.$$

How many three-digit natural numbers are there which have no zero digits in their decimal representation and satisfy the following condition: under any permutation of the digits of this number it remains such that it is not divisible by 4?
Find the smallest real value of the parameter $C$ for which the inequality $$\cos a+\cos b+3\cos a\cos b\le 2\cos^2 a+\cos^2 b+C$$ holds for all $0\le a\le b\le\frac{\pi}{2}$.

Call a natural number solidary if it is coprime to the sum of all its natural divisors.

a) What is the largest number of solidary numbers that can follow in a row?

b) What is the largest number of solidary numbers that can follow in a row if the number 1 is not considered solidary?

The incircle of a triangle $ABC$ touches its sides $AB$, $BC$ and $AC$ at the points $N$, $K$, $P$ respectively. It is known that $AB>BC$, and the bisectors of the angles $A$ and $C$ meet the line $NK$ at the points $Q$ and $T$ respectively. Denote by $S$ the point of intersection of the lines $AQ$ and $TP$, and by $F$ the point of intersection of the lines $CT$ and $PQ$. Prove that the lines $NK$, $SF$ and $AC$ meet at one point.
Find the largest natural number which is divisible by 7 and whose decimal representation contains only odd digits, the sum of which is 2015.

a) Andrii and Olesia each received a set of cards on which all the integers from 1 to 2015 are written. After that Olesia keeps some of the cards (but not all) from her set and puts the rest aside. Andrii does the same. In the coordinate plane the $2015^2$ points both of whose coordinates are integers from 1 to 2015 are considered. Olesia colours light blue those of these points whose first coordinate equals the number on one of her cards and whose second coordinate equals the number on one of Andrii's cards, and Andrii colours yellow those points whose first coordinate equals the number on one of his cards and whose second coordinate equals the number on one of Olesia's cards (some points may thereby be coloured in two colours). Prove that for any choice of cards they cannot achieve that each of the $2015^2$ points is coloured in at least one of the two colours.

b) Oksana joined Andrii and Olesia; she took all the cards that Olesia and Andrii had put aside. After that the three of them colour the points of a new clean plane as follows: Olesia colours light blue those of these points whose first coordinate equals the number on one of her cards and whose second coordinate equals the number on one of Andrii's cards, Andrii colours yellow those points whose first coordinate equals the number on one of his cards and whose second coordinate equals the number on one of Oksana's cards, and Oksana colours green those points whose first coordinate equals the number on one of her cards and whose second coordinate equals the number on one of Olesia's cards (again some points may be coloured in several colours). For which choice of cards by Olesia and Andrii will the three of them colour each of the $2015^2$ points in at least one colour?

In an acute-angled triangle $ABC$ the altitudes $AA_1$ and $BB_1$ meet at the point $H$. Construct two circles $w_1$ and $w_2$ with centres at the points $H$ and $B$ and radii $HB_1$ and $BB_1$, respectively. From the point $C$ draw tangents to the circles $w_1$ and $w_2$ which touch these circles at the points $N$ and $K$, different from $B_1$, respectively. Prove that the points $A_1$, $N$ and $K$ lie on one line.
Find all functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that for all real $x, y$ the equality $$4f(x+f(y))=f(x)+f(y)+f(xy)+1$$ holds.
Prove that for all natural $n\ge 2$ the number $$\frac{n^{1003}+n^{1002}+n^{1001}+1}{n+1}$$ is composite.

The bisector of the angle $\angle ABC$ of a triangle $ABC$ meets the circumcircle of the triangle at the point $K$. The point $N$ belongs to the segment $AB$, and $NK\perp AB$. Through the point $P$, the midpoint of the segment $NB$, a line parallel to the line $BC$ is drawn; it meets the line $BK$ at the point $T$. Prove that the line $NT$ bisects the segment $AC$.

The number 2016 is written on the board. Olesia and Andrii play the following game: they take turns (Olesia starts) decreasing the number on the board by a natural number not exceeding the number of the move (with the first move Olesia must decrease the number by 1, Andrii with his move by 1 or by 2, then Olesia by 1, 2 or 3, and so on). The player who manages to write the number 0 on the board wins. Who wins with correct play of both opponents?
Does there exist a function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that for any real numbers $x, y$ the inequality $$f(x-f(y))\le x-yf(x)$$ holds?

Solve the equation $x[x]=2016$.

Here $[x]$ denotes the integer part of the number $x$, that is, the greatest integer not exceeding $x$.

Until 1995, in the football championships of Ukraine in all leagues a team received 2 points for a win in a match, 1 point for a draw, and no points for a loss. From 1995 on they began to award 3 points for a win, while for a draw and a loss they gave, as before, 1 and 0 points respectively. The football federation decided to recount all the championships held in all leagues in all years according to the new scoring system, expecting that in principle the distribution of places would not change. But it turned out that in the 1927 championship, in one of the regional leagues, $n$ teams played a single round-robin tournament, that is, each team played each other once. Team "A" scored the largest number of points, and team "B" the smallest number of points. But after recounting the points according to the new rule, team "B" scored the largest number of points, and team "A" the smallest. For what smallest $n$ could this have happened?

The statement that a team scored the smallest or the largest number of points means that no other team scored the same number of points.

Call the degree of the number $n=p_1^{\alpha_1}p_2^{\alpha_2}\ldots p_k^{\alpha_k}$ the number $\deg(n)=\alpha_1+\alpha_2+\ldots+\alpha_k$, where $p_i$ are pairwise distinct primes and $\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \ldots, \alpha_k$ are natural numbers. Prove that there exist 2016 consecutive natural numbers among which there are exactly 1000 numbers of degree less than 11.

A triangle $APQ$ and a rectangle $ABCD$ are placed in the plane so that the midpoint of the segment $PQ$ belongs to the diagonal $BD$ of the rectangle, and one of the rays $AB$ or $AD$ is the bisector of the angle $PAQ$. Prove that one of the rays $CB$ or $CD$ is the bisector of the angle $PCQ$.

Do there exist 8 pairwise distinct integers $a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h$ such that the roots of the equations $x^2+ax+b=0$, $x^2+cx+d=0$, $x^2+ex+f=0$ and $x^2+gx+h=0$ are the numbers $a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h$ in some order?

An $8\times 8$ board is given. A genuine diagonal of this board is a diagonal containing at least three cells. Andrii and Olesia play a game on this board. They take turns (Andrii starts) placing identical counters on the board. It is forbidden to place two counters in one cell. If after some move it turns out that every row and every column contains at least one counter, Olesia wins. If after some move every one of the genuine diagonals contains at least one counter, Andrii wins. If after some move the victory of Andrii and of Olesia occur simultaneously, a draw is declared. Can one of the players secure a win for himself or herself if each strives to win?

In an acute-angled triangle $ABC$, $\angle ACB=45^\circ$, $M$ is the point of intersection of the medians and $O$ is the circumcentre. It is known that $OM=1$ and $OM\parallel BC$. Find the length of the side $BC$.

Let $d$ be a natural divisor of a natural number $m$, and let $(a_i)$ and $(b_i)$ be two arithmetic progressions with natural terms. It is known that there are indices $i$ and $j$ for which $(a_i, b_j)=1$, and also indices $k$ and $l$ for which $(a_k, b_l)=m$. Prove that one can choose indices $t$ and $s$ for which $(a_t, b_s)=d$.

Here $(x, y)$ denotes the greatest common divisor of the numbers $x, y$.

There were $12$ married couples at a party. The organisers numbered the couples with the numbers 1, 2, 3, $\ldots$, 12. At the end of the party it turned out that each of the 12 wives had drunk either 1 bottle of Coca-Cola or none. Each husband drank $2^ka_k$ bottles of Coca-Cola, where $a_k$ is the number of bottles drunk by his wife and $k$ is the number of this couple. It is known that the husbands drank 2018 bottles in total. How many married couples did not drink a single bottle of Coca-Cola?

A convex polygon $A_1A_2\ldots A_{2017}$ is given. Consider the following 2017 angles: $\angle A_{1009}A_1A_{1010}$, $\angle A_{1010}A_2A_{1011}$, $\ldots$, $\angle A_{1008}A_{2017}A_{1009}$. The largest of these angles is chosen. What is the smallest value it can take?

A natural number $n\ge 3$ is given. Olesia plays the following game: at the beginning of the game a counter is located at the origin of the Cartesian plane $XOY$. Olesia moves the counter according to the following rules: the counter may be moved in the plane only parallel to the coordinate axes. At the first step the counter must be moved by the distance $1=2^0$, at the second step by the distance $2=2^1$, at the third step by the distance $4=2^2$, and so on (the displacement of the counter at each new step is twice as long as at the previous step). In total Olesia makes $n$ steps. Her loss in this game equals the maximal distance from the counter to the origin during the whole game (not necessarily after the $n$-th step). What is the smallest loss Olesia can achieve?

For positive numbers $a, b, c$ prove the inequality $$\frac{(a-b)^2}{ab}+\frac{(b-c)^2}{bc}+\frac{(c-a)^2}{ac}+\frac ca+\frac ab+\frac bc\ge\frac{3bc+ac-ab}{2ab+ac}+\frac{3ac+ab-bc}{2bc+ab}+\frac{3ab+bc-ac}{2ac+bc}.$$
Solve in natural numbers $x, y, p, n, k$ the system of equations $$\begin{cases}5x+y=p^k,\\ 5y+x=p^{k+n}.\end{cases}$$

An isosceles obtuse triangle $ABC$ with apex at the point $B$ is given. The perpendicular bisector of the side $BC$ meets the lines $AC$ and $AB$ at the points $K$ and $M$ respectively. Prove that the point symmetric to the point $A$ with respect to the line $BK$ lies on the line $CM$.
Find all functions $f:[0,+\infty)\to[0,+\infty)$ which for all non-negative $x, y$ satisfy the equality $$f(f(x)+f(y))=xyf(x+y).$$

A squadron is advancing on an island; it consists of $10$ powerful destroyers and also 20 small boats. They are all lined up in a circle, the distances between neighbouring ships being equal, and they approach the island in this formation. The island is defended by two torpedo boats, each of which has exactly $10$ torpedoes. The launchers on them are set so that the first one can fire all its $10$ torpedoes simultaneously at $10$ neighbouring targets, and the second one all its $10$ torpedoes at $10$ targets standing every other one. It is known that they fire simultaneously (so two torpedoes may hit some targets simultaneously). What is the largest number of destroyers that can certainly remain intact, whatever the defenders of the island do?
Positive numbers $a, b, c$ satisfy the condition $a^2+b^2+c^2+abc=4$. Prove that the inequality $c+ab\le 2$ holds.

$N$ natural numbers are given such that the greatest common divisors of all non-empty sets of these numbers (of one, two, three, and so on) are pairwise distinct. What is the smallest possible number of distinct prime divisors of the product of all $N$ numbers?

In a triangle $ABC$ a line different from the sides of the triangle and passing through the point $A$ meets the altitudes $BH_2$ and $CH_3$ at the points $D_1$ and $E_1$ respectively. The points $D_2$ and $E_2$ are symmetric to the points $D_1$ and $E_1$ with respect to the sides $AB$ and $AC$ respectively. Prove that the circumcircles of the triangles $D_2AB$ and $E_2AC$ are tangent.

From the natural numbers $2, 3, 4, \ldots, 2019$ one somehow forms $1009$ proper fractions, and then the largest of these fractions is chosen. What is the smallest value this largest fraction can have over all possible constructions of such fractions?

Andrii and Olesia take turns cutting squares of some sizes along the grid lines out of a $4000\times 2019$ rectangle. After each move a connected figure must remain. The player who cannot make a move loses. Who wins with correct play of both players if Olesia starts?

A figure is called connected if from any of its cells one can reach any other cell, moving through sides of other cells of the figure.

In an acute-angled triangle $ABC$ the incircle with centre at the point $I$ touches the sides $AB$ and $BC$ at the points $C_1$ and $A_1$ respectively. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $AC$, $N$ the midpoint of the arc $ABC$ of the circumcircle of the triangle $ABC$, and $P$ the projection of the point $M$ onto $A_1C_1$. Prove that the points $I$, $P$ and $N$ lie on one line.

Distinct natural numbers $a$ and $b$, greater than $1$, are given.

a) Prove that for infinitely many natural $n$ the number $s_n=a^n+b^{n+1}$ is composite.

b) Prove that there are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $s_n$ is divisible by $p$ for some natural $n$.

Find all natural numbers $a$ and $b$ for which the number $2^{a!}+2^{b!}$ is the cube of a natural number.

Recall that for a natural number $n$ the value $n!=1\cdot 2\cdot 3\cdot\ldots\cdot n$.

A parallelogram $ABCD$ is given. A circle passing through the vertices $A$ and $D$ meets the lines $AB$, $BD$, $AC$ and $CD$ for the second time at the points $B_1$, $B_2$, $C_1$ and $C_2$ respectively. The lines $B_1B_2$ and $C_1C_2$ meet at the point $K$. Prove that the point $K$ is equidistant from the lines $AB$ and $CD$.

In a country the government decided to set up transport links between cities, by railway or by air, in such a way that from each city one can travel directly to at most four other cities. Prove that the government can always choose the type of link for the corresponding pairs of cities in such a way that there are no three cities every two of which are connected by the same kind of transport.
For positive numbers $x, y, z$ satisfying the equality $\frac1x+\frac1y+\frac1z=3$, prove that the inequality $$(x-1)(y-1)(z-1)\le\frac14(xyz-1)$$ holds.
For which natural numbers $n$ is the number $n^n+1$ divisible by the number $n+1$?

An equilateral triangle with side $n$ is divided into $n^2$ small equilateral triangles with side length 1 (see the figure). At the very beginning one of them, which has no common points with the outer sides of the big triangle, was coloured blue, and the rest yellow. In one move one may choose any of the $n^2$ small triangles and change its colour and the colours of the triangles adjacent to it along a side (from blue to yellow and vice versa). Is it possible after several moves to make the whole board one-coloured?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/ua10_2020_1_p2_fig.png

Let $H_a, H_b, H_c$ be the feet of the altitudes dropped from the corresponding vertices of a triangle $ABC$, $H$ the orthocentre of this triangle, and $K$ the point symmetric to $H$ with respect to the line $BC$. The line passing through the point $H$ parallel to the line $H_bH_c$ meets the lines $AB$ and $AC$ at the points $X$ and $Y$. Prove that the circumcircles of $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle XYK$ are tangent.
For real numbers $a, b, c, d$ satisfying the condition $a+b+c+d=a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2$, prove the inequality $$(2-a)(2-b)(2-c)(2-d)\ge 1.$$

An increasing geometric progression of $5$ natural numbers satisfies the following condition: the square of the sum of the second and fourth terms is $100$ times greater than the sum of the first, the fifth and twice the third term of this progression. What is the largest three-digit number that can be a term of this progression?

An isosceles triangle $ABC$ with base $AC$ is given, $P$ is an arbitrary point on this base, and $T$ is the projection of $P$ onto $BC$. In what ratio does the symmedian of $\triangle PBC$ drawn from the vertex $C$ divide the segment $AT$?

The symmedian of $\triangle PBC$ is the segment $CS$, $S\in BP$, such that the ray $CS$ is symmetric to the ray of the median $CF$ with respect to the ray of the bisector $CL$.

A chessboard was divided into domino pieces, that is, into $1\times 2$ and $2\times 1$ rectangles. On each such piece a number was written equal to the number of domino pieces which have a common segment with it, not counting the piece itself. What is the smallest possible value of the sum of all numbers written on the chessboard?
Let $a$ and $b$ be distinct natural numbers such that $a^2+b^2+1$ is divisible by $2ab+1$. Prove that $2ab+1$ is a perfect square of an integer.

Oleksii and Bohdan play a game with two piles of pebbles. At the beginning one of the piles contains 2021 pebbles, and the other is empty. In one move each of the boys must take an even number of stones (greater than zero) from an arbitrary pile, after which he moves half of the taken pebbles to the other pile and removes the other half from the game. The player who cannot make a move loses. Who wins this game if both strive to win and Bohdan starts?

Denote by $P^{(n)}$ the set of all polynomials of degree $n$ whose coefficients are a permutation of the set of numbers $\left\{2^0, 2^1, \ldots, 2^n\right\}$. Find all pairs of natural numbers $(k, d)$ for which there exists $n$ such that for every polynomial $P\in P^{(n)}$ the number $P(k)$ is divisible by the number $d$.
For arbitrary positive numbers $a\ge b\ge c$ prove the inequality $$\frac{a^2+b^2}{a+b}+\frac{a^2+c^2}{a+c}+\frac{c^2+b^2}{c+b}\ge(a+b+c)+\frac{(a-c)^2}{a+b+c}.$$

In a triangle $ABC$ let the points $O$, $I$ and $H$ be the circumcentre, the incentre and the orthocentre respectively. The lines $AI$ and $AH$ meet the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ for the second time at the points $D$ and $E$ respectively. Prove that if $OI\parallel BC$, then the circumcentre of $\triangle OIH$ lies on the line $DE$.
Find all sets of $n\ge 2$ consecutive integers $\{a+1, a+2, \ldots, a+n\}$, where $a\in\mathbb{Z}$, in which one of the numbers equals the sum of all the others.

Circles $w_1$ and $w_2$ meet at the points $P$ and $Q$ and are internally tangent to a circle $w$ with centre at the point $O$ at the points $A$ and $B$ respectively. It is known that the points $A$, $B$ and $Q$ lie on one line. Prove that the point $O$ lies on the external bisector of $\angle APB$.

A sequence $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{2n}$ of integers is such that every number occurs in it at most $n$ times. Prove that there exist two strictly increasing sequences of indices $b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n$ and $c_1, c_2, \ldots, c_n$ such that every natural number of the set $\{1, 2, \ldots, 2n\}$ occurs in exactly one of these two sequences, and for every $1\le i\le n$ the condition $a_{b_i}\ne a_{c_i}$ holds.

A natural number $n$ is given. Prove that one can choose $\varphi(n)+1$ (not necessarily distinct) divisors of $n$ with sum $n$.

Here $\varphi(n)$ denotes the number of natural numbers less than $n$ that are coprime to $n$.
A natural number $k$ is given. The product of some $k$ consecutive natural numbers ends in the number $k$. What values can the number $k$ take?

On a rectangular $100\times 300$ board two players take turns colouring cells that have not yet been coloured. The first colours in yellow, the second in blue. The colouring ends when every cell of the board has been coloured. A sequence of cells is a collection of cells in which any two consecutive cells have a common side (all cells in the sequence are distinct). We consider all possible sequences of yellow cells. The result of the first player is the number of cells in a sequence of yellow cells of maximal length. The aim of the first player is to obtain the maximal result, and the aim of the second player is to make the result of the first player as small as possible. Prove that if each of them strives to achieve his aim, then the result of the first player will be at most $200$.

Let $I$ be the incentre of a triangle $ABC$, and let $P$ be an arbitrary point taken on the arc $BAC$ of its circumcircle. On the tangent at the point $I$ to the circumcircle $\omega$ of the triangle $API$, points $K$ and $L$ are taken such that $BK=KI$ and $CL=LI$. Prove that the circumcircle of the triangle $PKL$ is tangent to $\omega$.

Let $(x_n)$ be a sequence of real numbers from the interval $(0;1)$. A sequence of natural numbers $(a_n)$ is defined as follows: $a_1=1$, $a_{i+1}=m$, where $m$ is the smallest natural number for which $[x_1+x_2+\ldots+x_m]=a_i$. Prove that for any indices $i, j$ the inequality $a_{i+j}\ge a_i+a_j$ holds.

In a convex pentagon $ABCDE$ the following conditions hold: $AB\parallel CD$, $BC\parallel DE$ and $\angle BAE=\angle AED$. Prove that $AB+BC=CD+DE$.

A pentagon is called convex if its diagonals lie inside the pentagon.

Let $P(x)$, $Q(x)$ and $R(x)$ be polynomials with integer coefficients satisfying the equality $P(x)=Q(x)R(x)$. Denote by $a$ and $b$ the maximum of the absolute values of the coefficients of the polynomials $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ respectively. Must the condition $b\le 2023a$ necessarily hold?

$n\ge 2$ pairwise distinct natural numbers are given. For each pair $a<b$ of these numbers the difference $b-a$ is considered. For each of these differences Vlada writes down the exponent of the highest power of two dividing it. What is the largest number of distinct numbers Vlada could have written down?

Consider a complete graph on $4046$ vertices whose edges are coloured in some colours. Call the graph $k$-nice if all vertices of the graph can be split into $2023$ pairs in such a way that among the colours of the $2023$ edges joining the vertices in the pairs there are exactly $k$ different ones. Could it happen that the graph is $999$-nice and $1001$-nice, but not $1000$-nice?

Solomiia wrote the numbers $1, 2, 3, \ldots, 2024$ on the board. In one move she may erase from the board any two numbers $a$ and $b$ and write instead of each of them their sum $a+b$. After some move all numbers on the board became equal. What is the smallest number of moves Solomiia could have needed for this?

A natural number $n$ is given. Find the smallest natural number $k$ for which there exists a collection of natural numbers $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_k$ for which the equality $$2^{a_1}+2^{a_2}+\cdots+2^{a_k}=2^n-n+k$$ holds.

In an acute-angled triangle $ABC$ the altitudes $AH_A$, $BH_B$ and $CH_C$ are drawn; they meet at the point $H$, and the point $M$ is the midpoint of the side $AC$. The bisector $BL$ of the triangle $\triangle ABC$ meets the segment $H_AH_C$ at the point $K$. The line parallel to $HM$ and passing through the point $L$ meets the line $BH_B$ at the point $T$. Prove that $TK=TL$.
Find all functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that for arbitrary $x, y\in\mathbb{R}$ the equality $$f(x)f(yf(x))+yf(xy)=xf(xy)+y^2f(x)$$ holds.
For arbitrary real numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ and $d$ from the interval $[0;1]$ find the largest possible value of the expression $a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2-ab-bc-cd-ad$.

Inside a quadrilateral $ABCD$ with equal sides $AB=BC=CD$, points $P$ and $Q$ are chosen such that $AP=PB=QC=QD$. The line drawn through the point $P$ parallel to the diagonal $AC$ meets the line drawn through the point $Q$ parallel to the diagonal $BD$ at the point $T$. Prove that $BT=CT$.
Find all polynomials $P(x)$ with integer coefficients such that for every natural $n$ the number $P(n)$ is natural and divides the number $n!$.

A country has 2024 cities, some pairs of which are connected by two-way flights. For any pairwise distinct cities $A, B, C, X, Y, Z$ there is a direct flight between some city among $A, B, C$ and some city among $X, Y, Z$. Prove that one can plan a route $T_1\to T_2\to\ldots\to T_{2022}$ passing through 2022 pairwise distinct cities.
A quadrilateral $ABCD$ is given in which the point $M$ is the midpoint of the side $CD$. It turned out that $\angle BMA=90^\circ$ and $\angle MAB=\angle CBD$. Prove that $AC=AB$.

12 segments are given. It is known that they can be split into 4 groups of 3 segments so that a triangle can be constructed from the segments of each triple. Can these 12 segments always be split into 3 groups of 4 segments so that a quadrilateral can be constructed from the segments of each quadruple?
It is known about a natural number $n$ that some $d$ of its distinct divisors form an arithmetic progression. Prove that the number $n$ has at least $2d-2$ divisors.

It is known that a sequence of positive real numbers $(x_n)$ satisfies the relation $$x_{n+1}=x_n+\sqrt{x_n+\frac14}+\sqrt{x_{n+1}+\frac14},\quad n\ge 1.$$ Prove that the following inequality holds: $$\frac1{x_2}+\frac1{x_3}+\cdots+\frac1{x_{2025}}<\frac1{\sqrt{x_1}}.$$

2025 natural numbers are given such that the least common multiple of all these numbers is not a perfect square. Mykhailo in turn covers one of these numbers and writes down the LCM of all 2024 numbers that remain uncovered. What is the largest number of the 2025 numbers written down that can be perfect squares?
Find all triples of non-negative real numbers $(x, y, z)$ satisfying the equality $$\frac{(x^2-y)(1-y)}{(x-y)^2}+\frac{(y^2-z)(1-z)}{(y-z)^2}+\frac{(z^2-x)(1-x)}{(z-x)^2}=3.$$

1000 numbers $2$ and 2000 numbers $-1$ are written in a row in some order. Mykhailo counted the number of groups of consecutive numbers consisting of at least two numbers whose sum equals $0$.

a) Find the smallest possible value of this number.

b) Find the largest possible value of this number.

In an acute-angled triangle $ABC$ ($AC>BC$) with altitude $AD$ the following points are marked: $H$ is the orthocentre, $O$ the circumcentre, $K$ the midpoint of the side $AB$. Inside $\triangle ADC$ there is a point $P$ for which the equality $\angle KPD+\angle ACB=2\angle OPH=180^\circ$ holds. Prove that $BH=2PD$.

Numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ and $d$ are given, each of which has exactly 2026 non-zero digits after the decimal point. Denote by $x_{(n)}$ the rounding of the number $x$, according to the rounding rules, to the $n$-th digit after the decimal point, for $n=1, 2, 3, \ldots, 2026$. Can it happen that:

a) $a_{(1)}+b_{(1)}>c_{(1)}+d_{(1)}$, $a_{(2)}+b_{(2)}<c_{(2)}+d_{(2)}$ and $a_{(3)}+b_{(3)}>c_{(3)}+d_{(3)}$?

b) for even $n$ the inequality $a_{(n)}+b_{(n)}<c_{(n)}+d_{(n)}$ holds, and for odd $n$ the inequality $a_{(n)}+b_{(n)}>c_{(n)}+d_{(n)}$ holds?

A triangle $ABC$ is given; on its sides $AB$ and $AC$ the points $E$ and $D$ respectively are chosen such that $DE\parallel BC$. Inside $\triangle ABC$ a point $F$ is marked such that $BE=BF$ and $CD=CF$. Prove that the line $AF$ passes through the circumcentre of $\triangle DEF$.

Vadym has $n$ blue and $n$ yellow counters. At the beginning all counters were shuffled and laid out in two rows of $n$ counters: the upper and the lower row. In one move Vadym is allowed to choose an arbitrary natural number $1\le k\le n$ and perform one of the following two operations:

- swap any two neighbouring counters in the lower row;

- swap the $k$-th counter of the upper row and the $k$-th counter of the lower row.

In what smallest possible number of moves can Vadym be guaranteed to achieve that all yellow counters are in the upper row and all blue ones in the lower row?

Does there exist a prime number $p>3$ and a permutation $\{a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{p-1}\}$ of the numbers $\{1, 2, \ldots, p-1\}$ such that the numbers $$\left\{a_1^{a_2}, a_2^{a_3}, \ldots, a_{p-2}^{a_{p-1}}, a_{p-1}^{a_1}\right\}$$ give pairwise distinct remainders upon division by $p$?
Prove that for every natural number $n$ there exists a natural number which is divisible by $n$ and has an odd sum of digits.

Petryk and Vasyl play a game on a square $4\times 4$ board consisting of 16 $1\times 1$ cells. Before the game starts, Petryk draws walls on this board at his discretion. Walls are unit segments that are sides of the $1\times 1$ cells. All segments of the outer boundary of the $4\times 4$ board are also walls. After that Vasyl places a counter in an arbitrary cell of the board at his discretion. Petryk does not see the board and does not know where Vasyl placed the counter, but he always remembers which walls he built there. After that the game begins. All of Petryk's moves are associated with four directions: up, down, left and right. By the rules of the game the counter can move to the neighbouring cell in one of these directions provided there is no wall between the cells. Each move of Petryk proceeds as follows: before his move Vasyl tells Petryk all those of the four directions in which the counter can move from the current cell to a neighbouring one. After that Petryk names one of the available directions and Vasyl moves the counter to the neighbouring cell in the direction named by Petryk, if this is possible. Then a new move of Petryk begins. What is the smallest number of moves after which Petryk can be guaranteed to determine the cell of the board in which Vasyl placed the counter at the beginning of the game?

In a triangle $ABC$ the median $AM$ is drawn, and the line $AM$ meets the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ for the second time at the point $N$. Points $X$ and $Y$ are chosen on the line $BC$ in such a way that the point $B$ lies on the segment $CX$, the point $C$ lies on the segment $BY$, and the equalities $\angle ABN=2\angle AXN$ and $\angle ACN=2\angle AYN$ hold. Prove that $BX=CY$.
Find all functions $f:(0,+\infty)\to(0,+\infty)$ such that for arbitrary positive $x, y$ the equality $$f(x)f(y)+yf(x+1)=2f(xy)+f(f(y))$$ holds.
